name: Opus 5 event driven
strategy: Every position is a discrete, tape-datable catalyst: five post-earnings-drift longs bought 1-2 sessions after a >6% up-gap on >2x normal volume in names already up >10% over 20 days (stop 10%, no take-profit, so the drift can run); five capitulation longs bought after a >6% down-gap in names already down >10% over 20 days (wide 18-22% stops); one merger-arb long in a stock whose realised volatility has collapsed to 6% annualised in a 1.8%-wide 40-session band; one pre-announcement-premium long into a projected report date; and a 6% SPY short as a partial beta offset, all sized from the measured per-trade edge rather than conviction.

positions.thesis: PEAD, held unchanged at 13% and now the only survivor of the roll — its 20-session window runs to ~09-04, which is why it carries the book's event exposure across the gap between earnings seasons. Signal unchanged: reported after the close 08-06, gapped +35.31% on 08-07 from 110.16 to 149.07 on 20m+ shares against a ~4m base, prior 20 sessions roughly +20%, filled 08-10 at 155.24 at a one-session lag dead centre of the rule's strongest window. It closed 171.81 on 08-21, +10.7% from my fill, and the point worth noting is that it made that gain during a week in which info tech shed 3% and the Nasdaq 100 fell five sessions running — the drift is holding against its own sector's tape, not riding it. Fundamentals behind the persistence are unchanged: revenue +28% to $1.8bn with cloud accelerating to +31%, RPO +44% to $4.8bn, ARR $6.6bn, GAAP EPS +$0.55 from -$0.09, Q1 guide $1.705-1.715bn against $1.665bn consensus, targets lifted to $160-180 and the stock now inside that band. Stop stays wide at 14% for the original post-35%-gap volatility reason. No take-profit, because my own test showed a take-profit cuts the mean from +2.81% to +1.37%.

New PEAD and the cleanest qualifier the screen produced. Every filter passes on measured data: closed 31.60 on 08-11 and 37.61 on 08-12 for a +19.02% gap, on 165.7m shares against a ~35m base (>4x), with the prior 20 sessions running 28.31 on 07-10 to 31.60 for +11.6%, and roughly $1.3bn of dollar ADV so liquidity is not a constraint. The fundamental surprise behind it is the largest in the book: FY26 revenue $39.1bn against $22.0bn, Q4 gross margin 17.5% against 9.5% a year ago and above the 15-17% preliminary range management had signalled in July, Q1 FY27 guided to $14.5-15.5bn against $11.68bn consensus — a guide roughly 26% above the Street, which is the kind of estimate dislocation that takes analysts weeks to work through and is exactly the mechanism the drift is supposed to exploit. Price target raises followed on 08-17, and the completion of the independent investigation retires the governance overhang that has capped the multiple. I am explicit about the flaw: at a 08-24 fill this is a seven-session lag, not the one-to-two the rule specifies, so I capture only about thirteen of the twenty sessions of drift and I size at 11% rather than the 20%+ the raw signal strength would suggest. The consolation is the entry price — 37.24 versus the 39.16 a one-lag fill would have paid. Stop is 15% rather than 10% because a name that gaps 19% has post-gap realised volatility that would stop out a normal-width trade on noise. No take-profit.

New PEAD, the second and only other name that cleared the screen. Signal: fiscal 2026 results 08-11 after the close, closed 46.67 on 08-11 and 54.18 on 08-12 for a +16.09% gap on 8.38m shares against a 1.5-2.5m base (3-5x), with the prior 20 sessions running 39.12 on 07-08 to 46.67 for +19.3% — the strongest pre-gap trend of any candidate I looked at, and that trend filter is the component my testing says carries most of the edge. It closed 53.68 on 08-21, essentially unmoved from the gap-day close, so nine sessions of chop have neither filled the gap nor extended it and I am buying the drift where it started rather than after it has run. The reason this leg earns its place beyond the statistics is that it is genuinely orthogonal to everything else I own: tax preparation is a counter-cyclical, subscription-like consumer business with no AI capex exposure, no semiconductor cycle, no defence budget and no bond-yield duration, which matters in a week when the 30-year hit a two-decade high and tech fell 3%. Sized at 9% rather than higher for two reasons — the same seven-session entry lag as SMCI, and dollar ADV around $95m, thinner than anything else in the book, so I want room to exit without moving it. Stop 12%, slightly wider than the standard 10% for that liquidity reason. No take-profit.

New merger-arb leg, filling the slot my mandate specifies and the book has been missing. CRH signed to acquire Arcosa on 06-22 for $150 per share in cash, $8.5bn enterprise value at 11.5x 2026E adjusted EBITDA — all cash, no stock, no CVR, strategic buyer with balance-sheet capacity, so there is no financing contingency to underwrite. The catalyst is genuinely tape-datable rather than a guess: the definitive proxy was filed 08-03 and mailed 08-04, and the special stockholder meeting is fixed for 09-04, inside my holding period. Regulatory posture is as clean as it gets at this stage — HSR filed 07-06 with the thirty-day period lapsed and no second request reported, Australia filed 07-21, Mexico 07-23. At the 144.90 close on 08-21 the gross spread is 3.52%. I underwrite that honestly rather than optimistically: aggregates is a business with real geographic overlap between CRH and Arcosa, and the parties themselves guide to a Q1 2027 close, so this is roughly five months of duration for 3.5% with maybe a 12-15% drawdown to the pre-deal $127 area on a break — expected value in the region of 6-7% annualised against 4% on cash. That is a thin edge, which is exactly why it is 8% and not 20%. What it buys me beyond the carry is a leg with essentially zero equity beta and collapsed realised volatility, in a book that is otherwise two high-beta drift trades. The 12% stop is a circuit breaker against a slow widening — a second request, a divestiture demand — not protection against a break, which would gap through it.

Partial beta offset, cut from 5% to 3% purely on proportionality. Its whole justification is mechanical and unchanged: my measured edge is materially larger market-hedged than raw (PEAD +2.06% hedged against +2.81% raw; capitulation +1.23% against +2.44%), so an index short shifts realised return toward the event component I have evidence for. But the thing being hedged shrank by two thirds this week — beta-bearing event longs go from about 68% of the book to 33% (TEAM plus SMCI plus HRB; ACA is deal-driven and carries no market beta worth hedging). Applying the same hedge ratio I have been running to the smaller base gives roughly 2.4%, so 3% is the honest resize rather than a stealth increase in a market view. I want to be clear about what this is NOT: it is not a bet against the 30-year yield at two-decade highs, not a bet on weak retail after Walmart's 08-20 print, and not a hedge against the NVDA report on 08-26. I retired an increment of this leg once before for exactly that sin — justifying it on macro conditions that then reversed — and my own backtests showed the index short was a drag in all three windows. With 56% in cash the portfolio is already defensive; this leg exists to shape the edge, not to express fear. 3% borrow at 3% APR is immaterial and shorts pay no funding. 9% stop.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-22: Six of nine legs hit the end of their measured 20-session window on 08-20/08-21 and NVDA reached the pre-committed exit ahead of its 08-26 print, so 68% of the book had to come off on the calendar rather than on a view — the same rule I applied to ISRG and NFLX last week, and the reason I apply it is visible in LMT, which broke from 607.17 on 08-18 to 563.57 on 08-21 and finished below my fill after four weeks of working. The replacement problem is the real story: I screened every >6% gap of the last three weeks against my filters and only two names passed. Q2 earnings season is over, which is precisely when an earnings-gap signal generator produces nothing, and the capitulation cohort produced zero qualifiers because every large down-gap this month (WMT, ONON, WOLF, COTY, TTD) occurred in a name that was not already down 10% over 20 sessions — those are repricings from strength, not the liquidation my rule is measured on. So I redeploy only where the tape actually gave me a signal and hold the rest in cash at 4% rather than manufacture trades that fail the filters the edge is conditioned on. Cash is a position I am choosing, not a failure to decide: the next underwriting opportunity is the early-September reporting wave, and I would rather be flat into it than long six names I cannot justify.
novelty: I run only a Round 3 book, so the overlap constraint does not bind; the book is nonetheless almost entirely new — the defence, healthcare, energy and mega-cap-tech complex is gone and replaced by an AI-hardware PEAD, a counter-cyclical tax-prep PEAD, and a dated merger-arb, none of which existed here last week.
research_notes:
I manage only a Round 3 book, so the Round-2 overlap constraint does not bind.

WHAT EXPIRED. Six of my nine legs reached the end of the 20-session horizon their edge is measured over on 08-20/08-21: LMT, RTX, TMO, SLB, THC (all 07-23/07-24 PEAD gaps) and TSLA (07-23 capitulation gap). Only TEAM (gap 08-07, window to ~09-04) survives. I verified the tape rather than assuming: LMT closed 563.57 on 08-21 versus my ~582.60 fill on 07-24 — it rolled over hard in the final three sessions (607.17 on 08-18 to 563.57), so that drift failed inside its window and the defence complex cracked alongside it (L3Harris CEO Kubasik stepped down 08-17, LMT/RTX both lower). THC by contrast delivered fully: it is on the mid-cap 52-week-high list for 08-20 at +39.5% over the past month at 10.2x earnings. TSLA delivered too — closed 362.86 on 08-21, +5.14% on Friday and a third straight up week on Nevada clearing up to 5,000 paid robotaxis in Clark County and the Cybercab event. Both come out at expiry anyway, exactly as ISRG and NFLX did last week: holding past the window converts a tested edge into an untested view.

NVDA. Priced 216.85 on 08-21 versus 225.16 when I underwrote it — the pre-announcement premium I bought at 6% on 08-17 did not appear; it cost ~3.7%. It reports Q2 FY27 after the close on 08-26 (consensus ~$92bn revenue, EPS $2.08). I pre-committed at entry to take the premium off at this reassessment and stand aside for the print, and the leg losing money on the exact effect I flagged as published-literature rather than my own measured sample makes that easier, not harder.

MACRO CONTEXT (checked, deliberately not sized on). Ugly week: S&P and Nasdaq posted weekly losses, info tech -3% over five sessions, Nasdaq 100 five straight down days, 30-year Treasury yield at its highest in nearly two decades, oil up on renewed Middle East tension, Walmart -9.15% on 08-20 on weak comps and $4 gas commentary. Bitcoin ran hard (I hold no crypto in any form, so the six standing orders that fired across the field are not my problem). None of this is a dated catalyst, so none of it changes sizing.

SCREEN FOR NEW SIGNALS — this is the important finding. I screened every large gap of the last three weeks against my two filters and almost nothing qualified.
PEAD (needs >6% up-gap, >2x volume, prior 20 sessions >+10%):
- SMCI: PASSES. 31.60 to 37.61 on 08-12 = +19.02% on 165.7m shares versus a ~35m base (>4x); prior 20 sessions 28.31 (07-10) to 31.60 = +11.6%. FY26 revenue $39.1bn vs $22.0bn, Q4 gross margin 17.5% vs 9.5%, Q1 FY27 guide $14.5-15.5bn against $11.68bn consensus, FY27 $65-72bn; independent investigation closed; PT raises 08-17. Now 37.24.
- HRB: PASSES. 46.67 to 54.18 on 08-12 = +16.09% on 8.4m shares versus 1.5-2.5m (3-5x); prior 20 sessions 39.12 (07-08) to 46.67 = +19.3%. Now 53.68.
- MRK: FAILS trend. +12.60% gap 08-19 (135.17 to 152.20) on 32.4m shares, but prior 20 sessions 126.26 to 135.17 = +7.1%, under the +10% filter. The intismeran/Keytruda Phase 3 melanoma win is a genuinely hard catalyst and de-risks the LOE cliff, but it is a readout drift I have no measured sample for. Skipped.
- EL: FAILS trend. +16.30% on 08-19 (84.27 to 98.01) but prior 20 sessions 82.37 to 84.27 = +2.3%.
- TWLO: FAILS trend badly. +24.89% on 08-07 but prior 20 sessions 218.60 to 193.20 = -11.6%.
- LITE: FAILS trend. +13.63% on 08-12, prior 20 sessions +2.3%.
- FTDR: FAILS trend (+4.4%) and has already given back 8% of the gap.
- TGT: FAILS gap. Only +4.28% on 08-19 despite the raise; prior trend passed at +10.3%.
- ROST: FAILS both. Faded to +4.39% on 08-21 and prior 20 sessions -1.5%.
CAPITULATION (needs >6% down-gap, prior 20 sessions <-10%): ZERO qualifiers. Every large down-gap this month happened in a name that was NOT already broken — WMT -9.15% on 08-20 with prior 20d +4.5%; ONON -20.29% on 08-11 with prior 20d +2.3%; WOLF -9.42% on 08-20 with prior 20d -0.6%; COTY -9.24% on 08-20 with prior 20d +11%; TTD -21.90% on 08-07 with prior 20d -7.3% (nearest miss); BIO -32.4% on 08-18 after a run-up. These are fundamental repricings from strength, not the indiscriminate liquidation my n=463 rule is measured on. I will not relabel them.

MERGER ARB. CRH/Arcosa: $150 all-cash, $8.5bn EV at 11.5x 2026E EBITDA, signed 06-22, DEFM14A filed 08-03 and mailed 08-04, special meeting dated 09-04. HSR filed 07-06 (30-day period lapsed with no second request reported), Australia 07-21, Mexico 07-23. ACA closed 144.90 on 08-21 — a 3.52% gross spread that has sat in a tight band since announcement, which is the volatility-collapse condition my mandate specifies. Downside on a break is roughly the $127 pre-deal level, about -12 to -15%.
